title.narrative: Civil Aviation Development Investment Program, Tranche 3

description.narrative: The Tranche 3 will continue from Tranches 1 and 2, to establish a sustainable civil aviation network to support the economic growth of the country. Tranche 3 will further strengthen and sustain the operations of National Airports Cooperation (NAC), PNG Air Services Limited (PNG ASL), and Civil Aviation Safety Authority of PNG (CASAPNG). The national airports have low level of compliance with safety and security standards, creating risks of accidents and illegal movements of people and goods. The air-side runway pavements, terminal buildings and utilities are in poor condition.Tranche 3 will improve and upgrade nine national airports including pavement strengthening, runway extensions, security fencing, apron extensions, fire stations, traffic control tower and terminal buildings. In addition, runway lights at seven airports, runway security fencing at three other airports and new market sheds will be constructed for women to promote local artifacts.

Safe, more efficient, and more accessible all-weather air transport services in project areas.

At least 9 national airports certified to meet CASAPNG safety and security standards. (Baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Since 2018 significant progress was made under the tranche in procurement and disbursement. The Momote Airport Pavement Upgrade and Terminal Building and Mt. Hagen Pavement Strengthening and Upgrade both procured under advance contracting were completed around mid-2021. In Momote, all airside works were completed in 2019. The new Terminal building and a market stall were completed only recently in Quarter 3 of 2021 due to COVID-19 impacts that delayed the import of some material components for the new terminal building. The new Terminal building was commissioned for operation on the 25th April 2022. In Mt. Hagen, the airside works, the runway pavement strengthening and 300m extension and the parking apron were completed in Quarter 1 of 2021. On the land side, the ARFF building, and the Air Traffic Control Tower (ATC) were completed in Quarter 3 of 2021. There were delays also on the import of some materials for the buildings due to COVID-19 restrictions. Preparations are underway for the opening of the new facilities by the Government.
ADB in 2018 approved ten (10) major works packages and awarded nine (9) of these packages; for Gurney, Mendi, Vanimo, Wewak, Madang and Wapenamanda Airport Upgrades and a fencing package comprising 3 contracts for Kerema, Kiunga and Tari.
The package for Kavieng airport upgrade which was tendered in 2018 was recalled by the EA and went for rebid in Q2, 2019 after ADBs clearance. The security fencing package for Kiunga Airport also went for re-bidding after the initial signed contract was terminated when the contractor failed to mobilize. ADB reviewed and approved the BER for both packages in Oct 19. The contracts were signed in March 2020.
From the total of 12 major contract packages under the tranche, only five contracts (Momote, Mt. Hagen, Gurney, Kerema and Vanimo) were fully completed within the program duration. Gurney airport pavement upgrade and runway extension was the first contract to be completed and within its contract period. The Wewak airport pavement upgrade and new terminal building was descoped and only the airside works, 3 staff houses and a tractor shed were completed at a reduced scope. The new Terminal Building was taken off from the scope and will be undertaken when funding becomes available. Tari Airport security fencing was terminated and absorbed under the ongoing contract for the Tari Airport Upgrade and New Terminal Building under Tranche 2 of the MFF program.
Five (5) contracts (Mendi, Madang, Wapenamanda, Kavieng and Kiunga) remain to be completed and are currently ongoing. These contracts have each reached beyond 60 percent physical completion at the loan closing date and were transferred to the Government to complete under its share of financing since ADB loan funds were frontloaded as requested by the Government to ease its cashflow gaps.
A revised procurement plan submitted by the EA was reviewed and cleared by ADB in March 2019. The revision included the scope for the airfield lighting system under the ongoing civil works packages and replaced the Buka Airport upgrade with a new works package for Wapenamanda Airport New Terminal Building and Associated Works. The revised procurement plan was approved through PRS. In October 2020, the EA requested for another revision of the procurement plan to utilize the uncommitted loan funds remaining under the project. This was approved by ADB on 26 October 2020. Another revision to the procurement plan was approved recently in April 2021 which was done to reflect the changes in costs and the scope.
